editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The layout_mode semantics (keep/improve/optimize), the replace_only_if_better default, the block-size limits (nine, six, and 65/33/27 qubits) and the warning-and-leave-unchanged caveat all match the English, and "passes de transpilador com IA" and "mapa de acoplamento" are used the same way everywhere. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The optimality claim, the post-processing-only caveat and the warning about noise drift ([20]) all come through intact, so nothing here would mislead a learner. In [17], POVM is rendered as "medida de operador com valor positivo", which reads as an operator having a positive value. The concept is a measure whose values are positive operators ("medida com valores em operadores positivos"). The gender of "Qiskit Function" switches from "da Qiskit Function" to "do Qiskit Function" in [25], and [20] has the clunky repetition "resultar em resultados imprecisos".

examples.suggested: medida informacionalmente completa com valores em operadores positivos (IC-POVM)
examples.why: The PT wording suggests an operator with a positive value. A POVM is a measure whose values are positive operators.

examples.suggested: Isso pode levar a resultados imprecisos.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still smooth a few calques. "as tightly together as possible" became "o mais próximo possível" in [15] and [45], which loses the sense of time. "run it through a classical optimizer" became "executá-lo por meio de um otimizador" in [36]. "complexo QPU" in [28] should be "complexo da QPU". The meaning is faithful throughout, including the migration table notes. A few wording choices should still change. In [8], "eventualmente" is a false friend: in Portuguese it means "possibly/occasionally", so it weakens "users will ultimately need to adjust their code". Use "em algum momento" or "mais cedo ou mais tarde" instead. The rest of the page ("será removida") keeps the requirement clear, so a learner is unlikely to be misled. Smaller slips: "padrões de acesso mais planos" in [7] is a literal copy of "flatter access patterns", "nomeadamente" in [6] is European Portuguese in an otherwise Brazilian text, and "comprimento de leitura" in [14] translates readout length as a physical length when it is a duration.

examples.translation: e, em seguida, um passo heurístico que tenta encontrar o melhor layout
examples.suggested: e, em seguida, um passe heurístico que tenta encontrar o melhor layout
examples.why: Everywhere else in the file, a transpiler 'pass' is 'passe'. Here 'passo' (step) blurs it with the 'dois passos' in the same sentence.

examples.source: cancel any back-to-back CNOT gates
examples.translation: cancelam qualquer par back-to-back de portas CNOT
examples.suggested: cancelam quaisquer portas CNOT consecutivas
examples.why: Leaving 'back-to-back' in English is a calque that a native technical writer wouldn't use.

examples.source: Routing stage
examples.translation: Estágio Routing
examples.suggested: Estágio de roteamento
examples.why: The heading keeps the English stage name, but the body text says 'roteamento' and 'estágios de layout e roteamento'. Optimization and Translation have the same mismatch.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the cost caveats in [19] and [21], so nothing here would mislead a learner. The page is written in European Portuguese with "tu" ("segue", "tens", "utilizadores", "consola"), but in [24] the link text switches to Brazilian "você" ("Execute seu primeiro circuito em hardware"), so the register is mixed. The plan name appears in three forms: "Open Plan" in [0]/[3], "Plano Open" in [1]/[2] and "plano Open" in [21]. [4] drops "instead", so the text no longer says to follow Install Qiskit *rather than* this guide, and [22] "É recomendado que" is a calque.

examples.source: Follow the steps in the [Run your first circuit on hardware](/guides/hello-world) guide
examples.translation: Segue os passos no guia [Execute seu primeiro circuito em hardware](/guides/hello-world)
examples.suggested: Segue os passos no guia [Executa o teu primeiro circuito em hardware](/guides/hello-world)
examples.why: This link text uses Brazilian 'você' ('Execute seu'), but the rest of the page uses European 'tu'. The register is inconsistent inside one list.

examples.source: Upgrade from the Open Plan
examples.translation: Fazer upgrade do Plano Open
examples.suggested: Fazer upgrade do Open Plan
examples.why: The plan name is written 'Open Plan' in [0]/[3], 'Plano Open' here and 'plano Open' in [21]. It should use one form throughout.

examples.source: follow the steps in [Install Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit) instead.
examples.translation: segue os passos em [Instalar o Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit).
examples.suggested: segue antes os passos em [Instalar o Qiskit](/guides/install-qiskit), em vez deste guia.
examples.why: Dropping 'instead' loses the point that individual users should use that guide rather than this one. This is a dropped qualifier, and it only weakens the redirection slightly.

examples.source: It is recommended that you set up a cost limit
examples.translation: É recomendado que configures um limite de custo
examples.suggested: Recomenda-se que configures um limite de custo
examples.why: 'É recomendado que' is a calque of the English passive. 'Recomenda-se' is the idiomatic form.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The dynamic-circuit caveat in [7] ("não retorna resultados precisos para circuits dinâmicos") and the "not required" stylesheet note in [9] both survive intact. "Timing" is rendered as "tempo de execução" in [0] and [1] but as "tempo do circuito" in the linked guide title in [7] and [16]. "Tempo de execução" also leans toward "runtime/total duration", when the page is about the instruction schedule ("temporização"). "Circuit" is mixed: English "circuits"/"Circuit" appear in [0], [1], [7] and [16], while "circuito" is used elsewhere, sometimes in the same sentence.

examples.source: Visualize circuit timing
examples.translation: Visualizar o tempo de execução do Circuit
examples.suggested: Visualizar a temporização do circuito
examples.why: 'Tempo de execução' suggests total runtime, not the timing/schedule of instructions. It also clashes with 'Visualizar o tempo do circuito', the title used for the related guide in [7]/[16], and the English 'Circuit' is out of place.

examples.source: this method does not return accurate results for dynamic circuits
examples.translation: esse método não retorna resultados precisos para circuits dinâmicos
examples.suggested: esse método não retorna resultados precisos para circuitos dinâmicos
examples.why: Two lines earlier the same paragraph says 'circuito'. Using English 'circuits' here with a Portuguese adjective reads as a mistranslation.

examples.source: Visualize the timing of generated circuits by generating a figure
examples.translation: Visualize o tempo de execução de circuits gerados criando uma figura
examples.suggested: Visualize a temporização dos circuitos gerados criando uma figura
examples.why: It has the same runtime-vs-timing drift, plus an English plural noun inside Portuguese syntax.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. Core terms are consistent: qubits lógicos/físicos, gadgets, limiar, ponto de equilíbrio, and "gate" kept in English on purpose. A native editor would still smooth a few calques. "é assumida como perfeita" / "podem ser assumidas como perfeitas" copies the English passive; "presume-se" reads better. "Em hipótese" in [10] and "Talvez mais provável" in [12] are stiff. [8] also drops "safely" from "can safely be assumed", and [14] flattens "could potentially be" to "pode ser".

examples.source: these classical computations can safely be assumed to be perfect as well
examples.translation: essas computações clássicas também podem ser assumidas como perfeitas
examples.suggested: pode-se presumir com segurança que essas computações clássicas também são perfeitas
examples.why: 'ser assumida como' copies the English passive, and the qualifier 'safely' is dropped.

examples.source: Hypothetically speaking, one could attempt to come up with
examples.translation: Em hipótese, alguém poderia tentar desenvolver
examples.suggested: Hipoteticamente, poderíamos tentar desenvolver
examples.why: 'Em hipótese' is an unnatural way to open a sentence in technical Portuguese.

examples.source: Perhaps more likely, there could be errors that are localized
examples.translation: Talvez mais provável, poderiam existir erros localizados
examples.suggested: Talvez seja mais provável que existam erros localizados
examples.why: The adjective 'provável' is left hanging without a verb, so the sentence reads as a literal calque.

examples.source: could potentially be an important part
examples.translation: pode ser uma parte importante
examples.suggested: poderia vir a ser uma parte importante
examples.why: The English hedge 'could potentially' is flattened, which makes the claim a little stronger. Minor, not misleading.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful everywhere and nothing would mislead a learner. The Eastin-Knill statement, the Shor/Steane/Knill error-correction descriptions and the magic-state distillation steps all match the English, and the terms are consistent (gate, código estabilizador, estado mágico, destilador, estado gato). A native editor would still fix a few calques and grammar slips. "como este processo parece no nível mais alto" [61] is a literal rendering of "what this looks like". "poderia-se" [64] has non-standard pronoun placement. "que o código não consegue lidar" [30] is missing "com". "para $n$ sendo o peso" [71] and "alguns códigos selecionados para torná-lo assim" [60] are stiff.

examples.source: The following diagram illustrates what this process looks like at the highest level.
examples.translation: O diagrama a seguir ilustra como este processo parece no nível mais alto.
examples.suggested: O diagrama a seguir ilustra, em linhas gerais, como é esse processo.
examples.why: Literal calque of 'what X looks like'. 'como parece' reads as machine translation.

examples.source: For example, one could potentially use a surface or color code for error correction...
examples.translation: Por exemplo, poderia-se potencialmente usar um código de superfície ou de cores...
examples.suggested: Por exemplo, seria possível usar um código de superfície ou de cores...
examples.why: Standard Portuguese does not attach the pronoun after a conditional verb ('poderia-se'). The redundant 'potencialmente' makes it stiffer.

examples.source: ...a high-weight error that the code cannot handle.
examples.translation: ...um erro de alto peso que o código não consegue lidar.
examples.suggested: ...um erro de alto peso com o qual o código não consegue lidar.
examples.why: 'lidar' requires the preposition 'com'. As written, the relative clause is ungrammatical.

examples.source: Shor error correction requires a state like this for $n$ being the weight of the stabilizer generator being measured.
examples.translation: a correção de erros de Shor requer um estado como esse para $n$ sendo o peso do gerador estabilizador sendo medido.
examples.suggested: a correção de erros de Shor requer um estado como esse, com $n$ igual ao peso do gerador estabilizador medido.
examples.why: The doubled gerund 'sendo... sendo' copies English syntax and is awkward in Portuguese.

examples.source: This could actually be challenging for some codes selected to make it so
examples.translation: Isso poderia ser de fato desafiador para alguns códigos selecionados para torná-lo assim
examples.suggested: Isso poderia ser de fato difícil para certos códigos escolhidos justamente para que fosse assim
examples.why: 'torná-lo assim' is an opaque calque. The point that the codes are chosen on purpose to make measurement hard is hard to see.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The threshold condition (p < 1/C), the doubly versus singly exponential growth, the 3.23% Shor-code figure and the 0.1% to 1% estimate all survive intact, and nothing would mislead a learner. A few calques remain that a native editor would smooth out. "criticamente não de N" is a literal rendering of "critically" (use "crucialmente"). "recíproco de N" should be the more usual "inverso de N". "Em maior detalhe" should be "Em mais detalhes". The theorem's "statement" is given as "declaração" in [2], when mathematical Portuguese uses "enunciado", and the file itself uses "enunciar" in [5].

examples.source: but critically not on $N$, the size of the original circuit
examples.translation: mas criticamente não de $N$, o tamanho do circuito original
examples.suggested: mas, crucialmente, não de $N$, o tamanho do circuito original
examples.why: In Portuguese, 'criticamente' means 'critically' only in the sense of criticism or judgment. It does not mean 'crucially', so this is a calque.

examples.source: larger than the reciprocal of $N$
examples.translation: maior que o recíproco de $N$
examples.suggested: maior que o inverso de $N$
examples.why: Portuguese mathematical writing normally says 'inverso' for 1/N. 'Recíproco' is understandable but reads as translated from English.

examples.source: Here is a somewhat informal statement of this theorem.
examples.translation: A seguir, uma declaração um pouco informal desse teorema.
examples.suggested: A seguir, um enunciado um pouco informal desse teorema.
examples.why: The standard term for a theorem's statement is 'enunciado'. The file itself uses 'enunciar' in [5].

examples.source: In greater detail, in order for a logical error to occur
examples.translation: Em maior detalhe, para que um erro lógico ocorra
examples.suggested: Em mais detalhes, para que ocorra um erro lógico
examples.why: 'Em maior detalhe' is a stiff calque of 'In greater detail'. 'Em mais detalhes' is the idiomatic form.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through and nothing would mislead a learner. The Search procedure in [30]-[33] (the f(x)=1/0 branches, 'se existir alguma', 'com alta probabilidade') and the cost comparison in [23] are rendered accurately. Terminology is consistent: 'portas de consulta de fase', 'operação de Grover', 'registrador', 'medições da base padrão'. Two small naturalness points remain. In [16], 'não tem dependência da função f' copies the English 'has no dependence on' word for word; 'não depende da função f' is more natural. In [20], [31] and [32], 'output' is translated as 'produzir' ('produza a string resultante', 'produzir x'), which reads stiffly; 'retornar'/'devolver' is more idiomatic for an algorithm's output.

examples.source: Notice that the operation $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ has no dependence on the function $f$
examples.translation: Note que a operação $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ não tem dependência da função $f$
examples.suggested: Note que a operação $Z_{\mathrm{OR}}$ não depende da função $f$
examples.why: 'has no dependence on' is copied word for word; 'não depende de' is how a Portuguese technical writer would put it.

examples.source: so we can stop and output $x$.
examples.translation: e podemos parar e produzir $x$.
examples.suggested: e podemos parar e retornar $x$.
examples.why: 'produzir' for an algorithm's output is stiff; 'retornar'/'devolver' is the usual term. The same applies to entry [20] ('produza a string resultante') and entry [32] ('produzir "nenhuma solução"').

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The O(N) and O(√N) query counts, the "if one exists" caveat, the "not a promise problem" negation and both Figure definitions all match the source, and the core terms (porta de consulta, busca não estruturada, problema de promessa, superposição) are used consistently. A native editor would still fix three calques. [8] "contar com $f$ tendo nenhuma estrutura" copies the English gerund. [19] "faz $f$ avaliar para $1$" is a literal rendering of "evaluate to". [21] "onde garantimos que há exatamente uma solução" turns "we're guaranteed" (a given promise) into something we ourselves guarantee.

examples.source: we can't rely on $f$ having any particular structure to make it easy
examples.translation: não podemos contar com $f$ tendo nenhuma estrutura particular que facilite o processo
examples.suggested: não podemos contar com que $f$ tenha alguma estrutura particular que facilite o processo
examples.why: The gerund 'com f tendo' copies the English structure. Portuguese uses a subjunctive clause here.

examples.source: a string $x$ that causes $f$ to evaluate to $1$
examples.translation: uma string $x$ que faz $f$ avaliar para $1$
examples.suggested: uma string $x$ para a qual $f$ assume o valor $1$
examples.why: 'avaliar para' is a literal calque of 'evaluate to'. In Portuguese the function takes a value; it does not 'evaluate to' one.

examples.source: where we're guaranteed that there's exactly one solution
examples.translation: onde garantimos que há exatamente uma solução
examples.suggested: na qual temos a garantia de que há exatamente uma solução
examples.why: The passive 'we're guaranteed' (the promise is given to us) became active 'we guarantee'. A learner would still understand it, but the promise framing is clearer with 'temos a garantia'.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The spectral theorem, the argument that eigenvalues lie on the unit circle, and the phase-estimation statement (autovalor/autovetor, círculo unitário, 0,999 close to 0) are all faithful, and the register uses "você" consistently. Two orthographic slips need fixing: "matrizes Hermitianas" in [5] and [10] and "norma Euclidiana" in [53] capitalize adjectives that Portuguese writes in lowercase ("hermitianas", "euclidiana"). In [68], "deve ser considerada dentro de $1/1000$ de $\theta = 0$" is a literal copy of the English phrasing; "a uma distância de no máximo 1/1000" reads more naturally.

examples.source: we'll apply it to Hermitian matrices as well
examples.translation: também o aplicaremos a matrizes Hermitianas
examples.suggested: também o aplicaremos a matrizes hermitianas
examples.why: In Portuguese, adjectives derived from proper names are written in lowercase. The same slip appears in [10].

examples.source: Unitary matrices preserve Euclidean norm
examples.translation: As matrizes unitárias preservam a norma Euclidiana
examples.suggested: As matrizes unitárias preservam a norma euclidiana
examples.why: Same rule: lowercase for an adjective derived from a proper name.

examples.source: should be considered as being within 1/1000 of θ = 0
examples.translation: deve ser considerada dentro de $1/1000$ de $\theta = 0$
examples.suggested: deve ser considerada a uma distância de no máximo $1/1000$ de $\theta = 0$
examples.why: "dentro de X de Y" copies the English construction word for word. The meaning is clear, but it reads stiffly.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The global-phase example [16], the diagonal-matrix caveat [55] and the spectral-theorem argument [61]-[88] are all rendered correctly. The terminology is also correct and consistent: 'matriz de densidade', 'estado completamente misto', 'semidefinida positiva', 'autovalores', 'traço'. A native editor would still fix a few small things. [70] has the English calque 'se deixarmos A ser' where 'se tomarmos A como' is expected. [26] has an agreement slip, 'dado uma seleção' (should be 'dada'). [55] uses the stiff 'não é necessariamente o caso de que'. [64] capitalizes 'Hermitianas', which Portuguese writes in lowercase.

examples.source: if we let $A$ be a column vector $\vert\phi\rangle$ and let $B$ be the row vector
examples.translation: se deixarmos $A$ ser um vetor coluna $\vert\phi\rangle$ e $B$ ser o vetor linha
examples.suggested: se tomarmos $A$ como o vetor coluna $\vert\phi\rangle$ e $B$ como o vetor linha
examples.why: 'deixar X ser' is a literal calque of the English 'let X be'. Portuguese mathematical writing uses 'tomar X como' or 'seja X'.

examples.source: what we could hope to learn given a random selection of a state
examples.translation: no que poderíamos esperar aprender dado uma seleção aleatória de um estado
examples.suggested: no que poderíamos esperar aprender a partir de uma seleção aleatória de um estado
examples.why: The participle does not agree with the feminine noun ('dado uma seleção' should be 'dada uma seleção'), and the whole construction follows English word order.

examples.source: it's not necessarily the case that we're talking about a classical system
examples.translation: não é necessariamente o caso de que estamos falando de um sistema clássico
examples.suggested: isso não significa necessariamente que estamos falando de um sistema clássico
examples.why: 'não é o caso de que' is a stiff calque of 'it's not the case that'. The meaning is kept, but a native technical writer would rephrase it.

examples.source: density matrices are always Hermitian and therefore normal
examples.translation: matrizes de densidade são sempre Hermitianas e portanto normais
examples.suggested: matrizes de densidade são sempre hermitianas e, portanto, normais
examples.why: Adjectives formed from proper names are written in lowercase in Portuguese ('hermitiana'). The inserted parenthetical 'portanto' should also be set off with commas.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The proof steps, the uniqueness of the square root, the "necessary and sufficient" orthonormality condition, and the destructive vs. non-destructive caveats in [40]–[43] all match the English. What a native editor would change is phrasing. "Traced out" is calqued as "traçado para fora" in [11], [12] and [45], where "descartado (via traço parcial)" is the usual wording. "Workspace system" is left half-English as "sistema de workspace" in [3] and [12] instead of "sistema auxiliar". [12] also uses "reminiscente de" even though [3] already uses the more natural "lembra".

examples.source: and can imagine that it is traced out
examples.translation: e podemos imaginar que ele é traçado para fora
examples.suggested: e podemos imaginar que ele é descartado (tomando o traço parcial)
examples.why: "Traçado para fora" is a literal calque of "traced out". Portuguese technical writing usually says "tomar o traço parcial" or "descartar via traço parcial". The same calque appears again in [12] and [45].

examples.source: combined with an initialized workspace system
examples.translation: combinado com um sistema de workspace inicializado
examples.suggested: combinado com um sistema auxiliar (de trabalho) inicializado
examples.why: "Workspace" is left in English even though "sistema auxiliar" or "espaço de trabalho" are established Portuguese terms. It repeats in [12].

examples.source: is clearly reminiscent of a Stinespring representation
examples.translation: é claramente reminiscente de uma representação de Stinespring
examples.suggested: lembra claramente uma representação de Stinespring
examples.why: "Reminiscente de" is a stiff anglicism. [3] already uses the more natural "lembra", so this sentence is also inconsistent with it.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the Schmidt, unitary-equivalence, bit-commitment and HJW arguments, so nothing here would mislead a learner. Several English calques remain. "traced out" becomes "é traçado fora" [5] and "pode ser traçado para deixar X" [136]. "on Y alone" is rendered as "em Y sozinho" / "em A sozinho" / "informação quântica sozinha" [93, 113, 119, 124] where "apenas em Y" or "somente com informação quântica" would be natural, and "tensoriado" [135] is awkward. "density matrix" is split between "matriz de densidade" [5, 6, 9] and "matriz densidade" [66, 93, 97]. The hedge "can typically be generalized" loses "typically" [10], and entry [102] has a misplaced comma inside the math ("expressões$,r$").

examples.source: that leaves $\rho$ when $\mathsf{Y}$ is traced out
examples.translation: que resulta em $\rho$ quando $\mathsf{Y}$ é traçado fora
examples.suggested: que resulta em $\rho$ quando se toma o traço parcial sobre $\mathsf{Y}$
examples.why: 'traçado fora' is a literal calque of 'traced out'; Portuguese texts say 'tomar o traço parcial sobre Y'.

examples.source: a unitary operation $U$ on $\mathsf{Y}$ alone
examples.translation: uma operação unitária $U$ em $\mathsf{Y}$ sozinho
examples.suggested: uma operação unitária $U$ atuando apenas em $\mathsf{Y}$
examples.why: 'sozinho' calques 'alone'. The same pattern recurs in [113], [119] and [124].

examples.source: $\rho$ is a density matrix
examples.translation: $\rho$ é uma matriz densidade
examples.suggested: $\rho$ é uma matriz de densidade
examples.why: Earlier entries [5, 6, 9] use 'matriz de densidade', but [66, 93, 97] use 'matriz densidade'. Pick one form.

examples.source: can typically be generalized to more than two systems
examples.translation: podem ser generalizados para mais de dois sistemas
examples.suggested: podem, em geral, ser generalizados para mais de dois sistemas
examples.why: Dropping the qualifier 'typically' makes a hedged claim sound absolute.

examples.source: In these expressions $r$ is the rank of $\rho$
examples.translation: Nessas expressões$,r$ é o posto de $\rho$
examples.suggested: Nessas expressões, $r$ é o posto de $\rho$
examples.why: The comma sits inside the math delimiters, so the page renders ',r' with no space after 'expressões'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall, and no sentence changes a claim a learner depends on (the scale/quality/speed metrics, the Gross code figures, the Berkeley utility experiment and the error-mitigation caveats all come through). The clearest slip is in [22]: 'superconducting materials patterned on a silicon substrate' became 'materiais supercondutores padrão', which says 'standard materials' and loses the fabrication meaning. It should be 'padronizados/gravados'. The rest are small: [10] switches to imperatives ('Descreva', 'Reconheça') where the other objectives use infinitives, IBM Quantum is 'A IBM Quantum' in [28] but 'O IBM Quantum' in [42], [60] drops 'at one time', [45] rewrites 'expand' as 'clique no triângulo', and [67] reads awkwardly as 'circuitos máximos por segundo'.

examples.source: which is made from superconducting materials patterned on a silicon substrate
examples.translation: que é feito de materiais supercondutores padrão em um substrato de silício
examples.suggested: que é feito de materiais supercondutores padronizados (gravados) sobre um substrato de silício
examples.why: 'padrão' after a noun means 'standard'. This is a false-friend mistranslation of 'patterned': it states that the materials are standard and drops the idea that they are patterned on the chip.

examples.source: Describe how quantum computing performance is measured ... Recognize supporting benchmark metrics
examples.translation: Descreva como o desempenho ... Reconheça métricas de benchmark de apoio
examples.suggested: Descrever como o desempenho ... Reconhecer métricas de benchmark de apoio
examples.why: This objective follows 'você deverá ser capaz de:', and the other objectives in the list use the infinitive. The imperative breaks both the grammar and the parallel structure.

examples.source: was at one time called the "100x100 challenge"
examples.translation: foi chamado de "desafio 100x100"
examples.suggested: já foi chamado, em certa época, de "desafio 100x100"
examples.why: The translation drops the qualifier 'at one time'. The source says the name is historical and no longer used.

examples.source: speed (maximum circuits per second)
examples.translation: velocidade (circuitos máximos por segundo)
examples.suggested: velocidade (número máximo de circuitos por segundo)
examples.why: This is a calque: 'circuitos máximos' makes the circuits 'maximum' rather than their rate. Entry [31] already renders it correctly as 'número máximo de circuitos por segundo'.

examples.source: Optional reading — expand to read more about the experiment
examples.translation: Leitura opcional — clique no triângulo para ler mais sobre o experimento
examples.suggested: Leitura opcional — expanda para ler mais sobre o experimento
examples.why: The translation adds a UI detail (a triangle) that is not in the source.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The simulator-vs-hardware conclusion in [27], the convergence caveat in [24] and the cost caveat in [20] all come through intact. The problems are small. "Primitives" has two genders on this page: masculine "primitivos do IBM Quantum" in the heading [17] and the conventional feminine "primitivas do IBM Quantum" in [19]. In [12], "Vamos também definir ... novamente" says "again" twice. The Estimator primitive is lowercased to "estimador" in [18]. "Lembre-se que" in [10] should be "Lembre-se de que".

examples.source: Step 3: Execute using IBM Quantum primitives.
examples.translation: Passo 3: Executar usando primitivos do IBM Quantum
examples.suggested: Passo 3: Executar usando primitivas do IBM Quantum
examples.why: Uses the masculine 'primitivos', but [19] uses the conventional feminine 'primitivas'. The gender should be the same throughout the file.

examples.source: We will again define the cost function, but this always took a fully-built and mapped Hamiltonian as an argument
examples.translation: Vamos também definir a função de custo novamente, mas como ela sempre recebeu...
examples.suggested: Vamos definir novamente a função de custo, mas como ela sempre recebeu...
examples.why: 'também' and 'novamente' both mean 'again' here, so one is redundant and the sentence reads awkwardly.

examples.source: will thus be importing our Estimator (BackendEstimator) from `qiskit.primitives`
examples.translation: importaremos nosso estimador (BackendEstimator) de `qiskit.primitives`
examples.suggested: importaremos nosso Estimator (BackendEstimator) de `qiskit.primitives`
examples.why: Estimator is the name of a Qiskit primitive. Lowercasing and translating it hides the fact that it refers to the API class.

editor_note: In [59], "for one of the first times" becomes "pela primeira vez". The page now claims the BF-DCQO result was the first good result reported on more than 100 qubits, a historical claim the source deliberately hedges. The rest is faithful, with a few minor slips. There are two typos: "colindo" in [37] (should be "colidindo") and "contrabalanciam" in [54] (should be "contrabalançam"). "Expectation value" is rendered with the calque "valor de expectativa" in [55] instead of the standard "valor esperado". "Agreement" becomes "acordo" in [49], and the English interjection "E hey" is left in [73].

examples.source: good results are being reported on over 100 qubits for one of the first times.
examples.translation: bons resultados estão sendo reportados em mais de 100 qubits pela primeira vez.
examples.suggested: bons resultados estão sendo reportados em mais de 100 qubits, numa das primeiras vezes em que isso acontece.
examples.why: This turns a hedged claim ('one of the first times') into an absolute priority claim ('the first time'), so the learner comes away with a false historical fact.

examples.source: a minimum expectation value ... the Pauli-Z expectation value
examples.translation: um valor de expectativa mínimo ... o valor de expectativa de Pauli-Z
examples.suggested: um valor esperado mínimo ... o valor esperado de Pauli-Z
examples.why: 'Valor de expectativa' is a calque. The conventional Portuguese term is 'valor esperado'.

examples.source: by colliding particles at super high energies
examples.translation: colindo partículas em energias super altas
examples.suggested: colidindo partículas em energias altíssimas
examples.why: 'Colindo' is a typo, not a Portuguese word. The gerund is 'colidindo'.

examples.source: adding terms that counteract these unwanted excitations
examples.translation: adicionando termos que contrabalanciam essas excitações indesejadas
examples.suggested: adicionando termos que contrabalançam essas excitações indesejadas
examples.why: This is a misspelled verb form.

examples.source: you can still obviously see very good agreement between theory and data
examples.translation: você ainda pode ver um acordo muito bom entre a teoria e os dados
examples.suggested: ainda é possível ver claramente uma concordância muito boa entre a teoria e os dados
examples.why: 'Acordo' is a calque of 'agreement'. In a data/theory context Portuguese uses 'concordância'. The word 'obviously' was also dropped.

examples.source: And hey, your solution may not pan out, and that's fine.
examples.translation: E hey, sua solução pode não funcionar, e tudo bem.
examples.suggested: E olha, sua solução pode não dar certo, e tudo bem.
examples.why: The English interjection 'hey' was left untranslated. A native writer would use 'olha' or 'ei'.

editor_note: The translation is faithful, and a learner would not be misled by it. Terminology is consistent throughout ("utilidade quântica", "vantagem quântica", "portas de 2 qubits", "entrelaçamento", "tolerância a falhas"). A native editor would still fix a few things. "Quantum mechanical systems/description" comes out in the wrong word order as "sistemas quânticos mecânicos" and "descrição quântica mecânica" in [13] and [46]. The English idiom was left in the calque "pelos próprios bootstraps" in [37]. [40] has a missing preposition ("a barreira que estamos nos aproximando"). There are also two small shifts in meaning: in [11], "impossibly difficult problem" became flatly "um problema impossível", and in [56], "too difficult or costly" lost its "too" ("difíceis ou caros").

examples.source: can make predictions about quantum mechanical systems
examples.translation: podem fazer previsões sobre sistemas quânticos mecânicos
examples.suggested: podem fazer previsões sobre sistemas quântico-mecânicos
examples.why: Wrong adjective order; the standard form is 'quântico-mecânico' (same problem in [46]: 'descrição quântica mecânica').

examples.source: essentially pulling physics and computational technology up by the bootstraps
examples.translation: essencialmente elevando física e tecnologia computacional pelos próprios bootstraps
examples.suggested: essencialmente fazendo a física e a tecnologia computacional se impulsionarem mutuamente
examples.why: The English idiom was carried over literally with an English word; it means nothing to a Portuguese reader.

examples.source: this is the wall we're approaching
examples.translation: é essa a barreira que estamos nos aproximando
examples.suggested: é dessa barreira que estamos nos aproximando
examples.why: 'Aproximar-se de' needs the preposition, so the sentence is ungrammatical as written.

examples.source: is itself an impossibly difficult problem as far as we know
examples.translation: é, em si, um problema impossível, até onde sabemos
examples.suggested: é, em si, um problema extraordinariamente difícil, até onde sabemos
examples.why: The English says the problem is extremely hard. The translation turns this into a flat claim that it is impossible, which strengthens it slightly.

examples.source: many problems that are too difficult or costly even for cutting edge supercomputers
examples.translation: muitos problemas difíceis ou caros até mesmo para supercomputadores de ponta
examples.suggested: muitos problemas difíceis ou custosos demais até mesmo para supercomputadores de ponta
examples.why: Dropping 'too' ('demais') weakens the point that these problems are out of reach, not just hard.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing here would mislead a learner. The spin-swap discussion in [87] (α=0°, ±90°, ±45°, 67%) and the caveat about deeper circuits in [24] come through intact. There are some small editorial slips. [41] shortens "transverse-field Ising model" to "modelo de Ising transversal", dropping "campo" even though [0] and [40] use "Ising com campo transversal". [25] renders "array of spins" as "matriz de spins", which next to Pauli matrices reads as a mathematical matrix. [42] has the clumsy repetition "em termos de termos de Pauli". [13]/[15] use the masculine "o exponencial", where Brazilian math writing normally says "a exponencial".

examples.source: We here consider the 1-D transverse-field Ising model.
examples.translation: Aqui consideramos o modelo de Ising transversal em 1D.
examples.suggested: Aqui consideramos o modelo de Ising com campo transversal em 1D.
examples.why: Drops 'campo': the field is transverse, not the model. This is also inconsistent with [0] and [40].

examples.source: These lattices consist of an array of spins $\sigma_i$
examples.translation: Essas redes consistem em uma matriz de spins $\sigma_i$
examples.suggested: Essas redes consistem em uma cadeia (arranjo) de spins $\sigma_i$
examples.why: 'matriz' suggests a mathematical matrix in a text full of Pauli matrices. For a 1D lattice, 'cadeia' or 'arranjo' is the natural word.

examples.source: a sparse representation of an operator in terms of weighted Pauli terms
examples.translation: uma representação esparsa de um operador em termos de termos de Pauli ponderados
examples.suggested: uma representação esparsa de um operador como combinação de termos de Pauli ponderados
examples.why: The repeated 'em termos de termos' is a stiff calque of the English.

examples.source: The exponential of an operator can be most easily understood through its Taylor series
examples.translation: O exponencial de um operador pode ser mais facilmente compreendido
examples.suggested: A exponencial de um operador pode ser compreendida mais facilmente
examples.why: Brazilian mathematical writing normally uses the feminine 'a exponencial'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, including the coloring, ZNE/PEA and quantum-advantage passages, and nothing here would mislead a learner. In [42], "we do not (__should not__)" became "não devemos (e __não devemos__)", which says the same thing twice and loses the escalation from "do not" to "should not". "Gate" is rendered two ways: "porta RZZ" / "portas de rotação" alongside "gates $CX$" and "gates de emaranhamento" ([22], [24], [26], [44]). "Fake device" also appears as both "dispositivo fake" ([18], [44]) and "dispositivo falso" ([47], [49], [53], [54]). Smaller calques are "tempo de parede" for wall time and "É só isso para a introdução".

examples.source: we do not (__should not__) ask the transpiler to do qubit mapping and routing
examples.translation: não devemos (e __não devemos__) solicitar ao transpilador
examples.suggested: não pedimos (e __não devemos__ pedir) ao transpilador
examples.why: The translation repeats the same verb twice and drops the step from what we do to what we should do.

examples.source: the RZZ gate in general requires two $CX$ gates
examples.translation: a porta RZZ em geral requer dois gates $CX$
examples.suggested: a porta RZZ em geral requer duas portas $CX$
examples.why: The same sentence uses both 'porta' and 'gate'. 'Gate' is also used in [24], [26] and [44], so the term should be made consistent.

examples.source: Since the fake device has 28 edges
examples.translation: Como o dispositivo fake tem 28 arestas
examples.suggested: Como o dispositivo falso tem 28 arestas
examples.why: 'Fake device' is 'dispositivo fake' here and in [18], but 'dispositivo falso' in [47], [49], [53] and [54].

examples.source: It took 161ms in wall time.
examples.translation: Levou 161 ms de tempo de parede.
examples.suggested: Levou 161 ms de tempo real (wall time).
examples.why: 'Tempo de parede' is a word-for-word calque. Native technical writing says 'tempo real' or keeps 'wall time'.

examples.source: That's all for the introduction.
examples.translation: É só isso para a introdução.
examples.suggested: Isso encerra a introdução.
examples.why: This copies the English sentence structure and reads stiffly in Portuguese.
